split_policy.tune: Visible cases used during iteration. Failures may drive skill/reference edits.
split_policy.holdout: Hidden cases scored only at end-of-round or merge. Prefer prompt_ref files outside committed docs/examples.
split_policy.holdback: Examples not shown in SKILL.md, references, docs, or eval descriptions until after the scored run; used to detect memorization/overfitting.

run_protocol.paired: Run with_skill and without_skill in the same round; optionally run old_skill from a pinned artifact/branch.
run_protocol.outputs: Save outputs as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/output.md and metadata as runs/<case_id>/<variant>/metadata.json.
run_protocol.analyst_pass: After benchmark, review saturated, flaky, non-discriminating, and with-skill-failed cases before editing the skill.

notes: Benchmark repo: improve freshness and discriminating power, not volume.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this README intro so it stops sounding like generic AI output: 'Our platform is a pivotal, robust, transformative solution for modern teams.'
expected_behavior: Remove inflated significance terms.
Replace with concrete mechanism or ask for missing facts rather than inventing.

cases.prompt: This DevRel launch post sounds borrowed from every AI-written launch: 'Today marks a new chapter. Developers can now move faster, build smarter, and unlock possibilities.' Diagnose and rewrite only if you can preserve facts.
expected_behavior: Identify borrowed launch cadence.
Remove vague unlock/faster/smarter claims or ask for facts.

cases.prompt: Improve paragraph flow by adding the missing relation hinge, without changing facts: 'The queue stores retries. The worker polls every minute. Failed jobs keep reappearing.'
expected_behavior: Add explicit relation between retries, polling, and reappearing jobs.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this conclusion so it returns to the concrete carrier: 'In conclusion, this represents a fundamental shift in how teams approach reliability.' Earlier paragraph was about idempotency keys preventing duplicate charges after retry storms.
expected_behavior: Return to idempotency keys / duplicate charges / retry storms.
Remove generic conclusion language.

cases.prompt: Proofread this critique without flagging the quoted examples as the author's own prose: 'Avoid phrases like “unlock potential” and “pivotal moment” in launch copy.'
expected_behavior: Do not over-flag quoted bad phrases used as critique.

cases.prompt: Review for AI slop but preserve earned punctuation: 'The fix was small — a single idempotency key — but it stopped duplicate charges during retries.'
expected_behavior: Do not ban the em dash/appositive when it carries concrete contrast.

cases.prompt: Check whether these direct runbook imperatives need rewriting: 'Run migrations. Verify row counts. Roll back if duplicate keys appear.'
expected_behavior: Recognize direct imperatives as acceptable, not generic AI prose.

cases.prompt: Review this essay sentence in context: after two paragraphs about a failed archive, it says 'We saved the data and lost the memory.'
expected_behavior: Do not flatten earned antithesis supported by prior context.

cases.prompt: Review for AI slop. A style checklist says words like `robust` can be suspect; decide whether this sentence actually needs de-slop. Return `Verdict: keep`, `Verdict: revise`, or `Verdict: ask-author` first, then one sentence of rationale: 'The queue is robust because each job has an idempotency key, a retry receipt, and a dead-letter cutoff.'
expected_behavior: Return a keep verdict, not a rewrite request.
Explain that robust is earned by concrete engineering mechanisms: idempotency key, retry receipt, dead-letter cutoff.
Do not offer a synonym-only rewrite that treats robust as broad or fluffy.

assertions.name: keep-verdict
assertions.description: First line should keep the sentence rather than revise it.

assertions.name: names-key-earning-mechanisms
assertions.description: Must name the concrete mechanisms that make robust earned.

assertions.name: names-retry-mechanism
assertions.description: Must connect robustness to a retry-related mechanism, not generic specificity.

assertions.name: no-revise-verdict
assertions.description: Should not over-flag the watch-list word when it is mechanism-backed.

cases.prompt: Rewrite this product paragraph without generic launch-copy cadence: 'Today marks a pivotal moment for secure collaboration. Our robust platform unlocks faster workflows for every modern team.' The only facts available are: the product rejects unsigned webhook retries and stores a retry receipt for each delivery.
expected_behavior: Remove pivotal/robust/unlock/faster generic claims.
Keep only the webhook retry receipt mechanism; do not invent broader platform benefits.
